findings.summary: The line "Not on the stack, not all in the heap" is a cryptic fragment, and the metaspace and static-field facts under it are packed into one prose paragraph.
findings.evidence:
Not on the stack, not all in the heap
Class metadata lives in Metaspace (native memory, Java 8+). Static fields live on the heap, held by the Class object.
findings.fix: Replace the fragment with a clear label such as "Special cases". Add a small table or two one-line bullets: Class metadata → Metaspace (native memory); Static fields → heap, held by the Class object.

s += | n/a | many garbage objects
findings.fix: Use clear columns such as Approach | Thread-safe | Cost, and write "no (immutable, new object each time)" instead of "n/a".

findings.summary: The Diagnose section gives the steps and the hprof analysis before the commands, and the -XX heap-dump flag is mixed in between them in the wrong order.
findings.evidence:
Find the pid, check the heap, dump live objects
Open heap.hprof in Eclipse MAT or VisualVM
Add -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError to the JVM flags
bash
jps
jcmd <pid> GC.heap_info
jmap -dump:live,format=b,file=heap.hprof <pid>
findings.fix: List the steps in the order they run: jps → jcmd → jmap → open in MAT. Put the HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError flag in a separate "Automatic dump" bullet.
